title: Recover an ambiguous Supervisor namespace create without duplicating VKS provisioning
prompt:
Complete `VcfVksEnsure/VcfVksEnsure.psm1` as a PowerShell 7.4 module that safely ensures a vSphere Supervisor namespace and one named VKS Cluster API resource.

Read the protected `docs/contract.json` and `docs/official_sources.json` first. The focused vCenter contract was projected directly from `specifications/vsphere/openapi/automation/vcenter.yaml` in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository at the immutable VCF 9.1 commit recorded in both files. The YAML specification, not a rendered documentation page, is authoritative. Use exactly `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2` and `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_createV2`. The VKS route is separately identified as a Kubernetes resource operation and must not be given a fictional VMware operationId.

VCF PowerCLI 9.1 is installed by the environment. Keep the protected manifest prerequisite on the genuine `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` module version `13.5.0.25380678`. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, redefine, or replace VMware modules, SDK assemblies, bindings, specifications, or harness tools. Use `System.Net.Http.HttpClient` for the focused REST workflow; do not use `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, curl, a subprocess, raw sockets, or a live VMware endpoint.

Preserve the supplied `Ensure-VcfVksCluster` signature and export only that function. Construction of each call must validate both base URIs and both credentials before traffic. `VCenterBaseUri` is an absolute HTTP(S) URI whose path is exactly `/api`; `KubernetesBaseUri` is an absolute HTTP(S) origin with root path. Reject URI credentials, query, or fragment, and reject blank or header-unsafe credentials. Do not follow redirects.

The ensure workflow is name-idempotent and ordered:

1. Send a bodyless `GET` for the namespace with `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_getV2`. If it exists, require the requested Supervisor and `RUNNING` state. If it is absent, send `Vcenter.Namespaces.Instances_createV2` at most once in this function call.
2. The fixture commits that first namespace create but deliberately returns HTTP 503. Treat HTTP 500, 502, 503, 504, a connection failure, or HTTP 409 as an ambiguous create outcome. Recover only by probing the named namespace with `getV2`; never blindly repeat the POST in the same call. If a probe finds the compatible `RUNNING` namespace, continue. If all probes still return 404, fail with an outcome-unknown error that states no second create was sent. Any incompatible existing object is terminal.
3. Discover the exact named VKS resource with a bodyless Kubernetes `GET`. If absent, send its namespaced collection `POST` at most once. Apply the same read-after-ambiguous-write rule for HTTP 409, 500, 502, 503, 504, or a connection failure. Require any existing or returned object to be the requested `cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta2` `Cluster`, namespace, name, topology class, and version.
4. Return one object with exactly `Namespace`, `NamespaceCreated`, `NamespaceRecoveredAfterAmbiguousCreate`, `Cluster`, and `ClusterCreated`. Calling the function again with the same inputs must return both Created flags as false and must not issue either POST again.

Wire rules are exact. Percent-encode each dynamic path value as one UTF-8 RFC 3986 path segment. Send `Accept: application/json` on every request. Send `Content-Type: application/json` only with a nonempty JSON body. Send exactly one `vmware-api-session-id` header only to vCenter and exactly one `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header only to Kubernetes. Send no query string or trailing `?`, do not follow redirects, and do not expose credentials or response bodies in errors.

The namespace create body always has exactly `namespace` and `supervisor`. Add `description` only when a nonblank `NamespaceDescription` was explicitly supplied. Add one `storage_specs` item containing only `policy` only when a nonblank `StoragePolicy` was explicitly supplied. Omit every other optional `CreateSpecV2` field. The Cluster create body always has exactly `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, and `spec`; `metadata` has only `name` and `namespace`, and `spec.topology` always has only `class` and `version`. Add `spec.clusterNetwork` only when both `ServiceCidr` and `PodCidr` were supplied; reject a partial pair. When present it contains only `services.cidrBlocks`, `pods.cidrBlocks`, and `serviceDomain: cluster.local`. Never serialize an unset option as null, an empty string, an empty array, or an empty object.

Run `python3 -B .moonshiner/verify.py`. The protected verifier starts a contract-pinned mock on an ephemeral `127.0.0.1` port, generates the fixture identifiers and credentials at runtime, invokes the ensure function twice, and reads the mock's flushed and fsynced JSONL request log. The mock derives its complete route allow-list from `docs/contract.json` and serves no other operation. Verification checks exact ordered methods, raw targets, headers, bodies, omission of every unset option, credential separation, the single ambiguous-write recovery, and the absence of duplicate POSTs. No live VMware endpoint is contacted.

Everything under `.moonshiner/` and `docs/`, plus `VcfVksEnsure/VcfVksEnsure.psd1`, is protected. Edit only `VcfVksEnsure/VcfVksEnsure.psm1`.
scenario: the first Supervisor namespace create commits successfully but its response is replaced by HTTP 503; the client must recover by reading the named namespace, create the named VKS Cluster once, and make a later whole-operation retry read-only
constraint: the contract-pinned loopback request log proves that each named mutation is sent once, the ambiguous vCenter POST is never blindly repeated, and all unset optional fields are absent on the wire
